headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict: Haystack can feed unverified outputs into Transformers, while both have broad network/file/tool surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be bridged into Transformers through shared files or pipeline inputs. Transformers can read files and run subprocesses, making it plausible it will parse attacker-controlled content as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF Haystack output is copied into a Transformers prompt, config, or example script without sanitization.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is used between the two agents.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Haystack outputs into Transformers prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter and schema validator before any handoff.
Use a read-only staging file for inter-agent transfer.
Review one sample handoff for prompt-injection markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to every inter-agent message.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call MCP servers; Transformers can read and write the filesystem and also has broad egress. If both touch the same workspace, file contents can flow from Haystack into Transformers and then out over the network. The profiles do not show secrets handling, so the main risk is shared-workspace leakage rather than confirmed secret exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or mounted volume.
IF Haystack ingests files that contain sensitive data and Transformers processes or uploads them.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory.
Turn off network egress for one agent during transfers.
Inspect one recent output for accidental file echoing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem and network capabilities, and Transformers can write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages while Haystack can use MCP and broad egress. In a shared directory, concurrent writes or package changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles do not mention locking, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path.
IF either agent modifies package state or generated artifacts without coordination.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Make shared paths read-only.
Check for concurrent file modification timestamps.
requires-engineering: add file locks or an orchestrator mutex.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search/RAG agent, so its outputs are likely treated as retrieved facts. Transformers can then render, transform, or act on those outputs using scripts and subprocesses. Without a verification step, an error or hallucination in Haystack can cascade into downstream actions or documents produced by Transformers.
conditions: IF Transformers consumes Haystack retrievals as authoritative input.
IF no verification or citation-check step exists between retrieval and downstream use.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step.
Require source citations before downstream use.
Compare one output against the original source document.
Block action-taking until confidence thresholds are met.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Transformers touches text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: if the pair is used on regulated content, the broader data surface of Transformers may exceed Haystack's documented scope. The other agent is cited because the mismatch is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed through Transformers.
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two agents in deployment.
mitigations: Restrict the pair to non-sensitive data.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Review logs for unexpected payload capture.
Disable multimodal inputs unless needed.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both deployments.
